title: "Chapter 17 Lab: Project Toolkit — Phase 1"
subtitle: "Drafting Core Documents for Data Collection"
---

## Overview

This lab is **Phase 1** of the [Project Toolkit](project/project-toolkit.qmd). You will draft the core documents your group needs before data collection day. **Labs 17 and 18** complete all toolkit materials so you are ready for **data collection in Week 19**.

**Phase 1 (Week 17):** Draft Participant Information Sheet, Consent Form, Debrief Form, Participant Instructions, and **start** the Researcher Procedure.

**Phase 2 (Week 18):** Recruitment Script, Data Recording Sheet, finalise Stimulus Materials, **complete** Researcher Procedure, practice run, Research Study Order Form.

---

## Why These Documents Matter

Your group must prepare **9 documents** (see the Project Toolkit checklist). In Phase 1 you focus on the **participant-facing** documents and the beginning of the **Researcher Procedure**. These ensure:

- **Ethics**: Informed consent (Information Sheet + Consent) and debriefing (Debrief Form) are required.
- **Standardisation**: Participant Instructions and Researcher Procedure ensure every participant is treated the same way.
- **Replicability**: A clear procedure allows others (and your future selves) to run the study exactly the same way.

---

## Document 1: Participant Information Sheet

**What it is:** A formal document given to potential participants *before* they agree. It explains the study in general terms so they can give informed consent.

**Who sees it:** Every participant; they read it before signing consent and keep a copy.

**Tips:**

- Describe **purpose** and **what will happen** in plain language. Do **not** reveal your hypothesis.
- Include: time required, risks/benefits, confidentiality, right to withdraw, contact for questions.
- Use the toolkit template and customise the purpose and "what will happen" sections. Refer to the worked example for tone and length.

---

## Document 2: Consent Form

**What it is:** The form the participant signs to confirm they have read the information, understand the study, and agree to take part. A legal and ethical requirement.

**Who sees it:** Every participant signs one; you keep the signed copies securely.

**Tips:**

- Update the **study title** only if needed; the checklist items are standard.
- Use the **same study title** on every document (Information Sheet, Consent, Debrief, Procedure).
- Plan to print plenty of copies (e.g. 30) for data collection.

---

## Document 3: Debrief Form

**What it is:** A document given to participants *after* the study explaining its true purpose, including the hypothesis and relevant theory.

**Who sees it:** Every participant receives this after completing the study.

**Tips:**

- Here you **can** (and should) reveal the hypothesis and explain the theory (e.g. dual coding, anchoring).
- Include data withdrawal instructions and support service contacts.
- Keep it to about one page. Use the template and worked example.

---

## Document 7: Participant Instructions

**What it is:** A clear, step-by-step sheet telling the participant exactly what to do during the study (e.g. "Read the list of words", "You have 2 minutes", "Write down as many as you can remember").

**Who sees it:** Every participant reads this before the study begins.

**Tips:**

- Use **numbered steps** and plain language. No jargon; no hypothesis.
- Keep it short (about half a page). If your between- and within-subjects procedures differ, use separate instruction sheets.
- Do **not** reveal what you expect to find.

---

## Document 8: Researcher Procedure (Start in Phase 1)

**What it is:** A detailed step-by-step guide for the researcher running the study. Includes exact wording, timing, and the full procedure. Your "recipe" for running the study.

**Who sees it:** Researchers only.

**Tips:**

- **Phase 1:** Write the materials checklist, the sequence (greeting → consent → instructions → main task → debrief), timing for each phase, and exact words to say to participants (in quotes or italics).
- **Phase 2 (Week 18):** Complete with data recording, scoring, and any final details. Any group member should be able to run the study from this document alone.
- Use the template; refer to the between- or within-subjects example procedure in the toolkit.

---

## Preparation for the Lab

Before the lab:

- Re-read the [Project Toolkit](project/project-toolkit.qmd) timeline and document checklist (documents 1, 2, 3, 7, 8).
- Have your **research question**, **design** (between/within), and **main task** (what participants do) clear from your Research Plan.
- Download the relevant **templates** from the toolkit so you can start drafting in the lab.

| 7. Participant Instructions | Draft (numbered steps, no hypothesis) |
